clue.text: Limits local charges as carpet is rolled out

indicators.note: a carpet rolled out is spread and unfurled, hinting that these letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A remark on local charges being limited while a carpet is unrolled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled out' signals the anagram of AS CARPET; 'is' only links. Rate-capping was the British government's 1980s limit on what local councils could levy in rates, their property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Caps on rates were statutory ceilings imposed on the property taxes British councils could levy.

clue.text: Only final part of letter I sent gets answered quickly

indicators.note: only the final part of the word letter is wanted, so just its last character is taken

parts.note: to send a letter is to post it, so sent means posted

explanation.surface: Someone sends a letter and receives a swift reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter-and-post picture hides the mechanism: take R, the last letter of 'letter', then I, then POSTED for 'sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, so to have made one is to have retorted swiftly.

clue.text: Court case that really intimidates all lawbreakers, primarily

indicators.note: primarily, in the sense of first of all, tells us to take the opening character of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A court case that frightens every criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing of evidence before a judge and jury is the standard sense of a court case.

clue.text: See the mice scurrying about? That could be harmful to Cheddar etc.

definitions.text: That could be harmful to Cheddar etc.

indicators.note: mice scurrying about run every which way, which signals that the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Spotting mice running about, which might spoil the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurrying about' shuffles SEE THE MICE. Cheddar is a hard English cheese, so 'Cheddar etc.' means cheeses generally.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny arachnid infests stored cheese rinds and can damage them, so it threatens cheeses.

clue.text: Street gang crowding round? Charming!

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, so the gang sits inside the crowding word

parts.note: crowding someone is pressing in on them
posse is slang for a gang of youths on the streets

explanation.surface: A gang closing in around someone, met with an ironic exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container. 'Street gang' is slang usage: a posse is a band of youths, originally a sheriff's party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepossessing makes a favourable first impression, which is to say it is attractive and engaging.

clue.text: Awkward, being covered with 27

explanation.surface: An awkward situation for something coated with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the answer to 27-across, a glue. 'being' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is a tricky one; something smeared with glue is literally tacky to the touch.

clue.text: 16 not greeting film maker

indicators.note: not here means without, so the greeting is removed from the island

parts.note: the answer to 16-across, a South Pacific island
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A Pacific island minus a hello yields a director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes HI out of TAHITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was the French director and comic actor behind Monsieur Hulot's Holiday and Playtime.

clue.text: Savoury food and drink shortly after end of game

indicators.note: after the end of means coming once the game is over, so the drink follows the game

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the drink loses its final character

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Snacks and a cuppa once the match is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the drink and 'after end of' sets it after the game: tea once play is over. Croquet is an English lawn game played with mallets and hoops.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small fried roll of mashed potato, meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs, a savoury dish.

clue.text: Enemy's mistreated submissive types

indicators.note: something mistreated is knocked about, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enemy has abused people who just go along with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges ENEMYS; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with everything a superior says.

clue.text: Fantastic discount on pre-packed basmati, perhaps… thanks to these?

definitions.text: Fantastic discount on pre-packed basmati, perhaps… thanks to these?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another means it comes after it
packed means filled, so the rice goes inside the word pre

parts.note: taken as written from the first part of pre-packed
basmati is a variety of rice, so this is an example pointing at the general food

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the letters of discount are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shoppers find a superb discount on bags of basmati rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed' is the container signal and 'Fantastic' rearranges DISCOUNT to DUCTIONS; 'on' means after in an across clue. The whole clue doubles as definition: such cuts are what make a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering what goods cost is exactly what gives shoppers a big discount on rice.

clue.text: Surprise upset for United captain

indicators.note: something upset is overturned, signalling the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A football club's skipper suffers a shock defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' anagrams UNITED CAPTAIN; 'for' links. 'Surprise' is adjectival here, as in a surprise attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise event is one nobody expected or foresaw.

clue.text: She sells drinks in southwestern state

indicators.note: in signals that the drinks go inside the southwestern abbreviation

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for southwestern
ales are drinks
Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A woman selling drinks in a southwestern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'She sells' looks like the start of a tongue-twister but is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose job is selling goods to customers.

clue.text: One of the Calendar Girls?

parts.note: Calendar Girls is a film about women posing for a charity calendar, but read literally it means the months whose names are also women's names

explanation.surface: Asking about a member of the Calendar Girls troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Calendar Girls is a British film about Yorkshire women who posed nude for a charity calendar; here it means a month that doubles as a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth month of the year is also a common girl's first name.

clue.text: Measure most of floor in one of several shops

parts.note: a chain is an old unit of length, 22 yards

indicators.note: most of means the final character of the word for floor is dropped

parts.note: a storey is a floor of a building

explanation.surface: Measuring nearly all of a floor in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old British unit of length (22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch). 'most of' cuts STOREY to STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch belonging to a retail group with many outlets under one name.

clue.text: Scholar recalled problems in maths and a religion lesson

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole string is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Remembering school sums and a religious studies class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SUMS A RE backwards. RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a celebrated Renaissance humanist and Dutch man of learning.

clue.text: Terrible actor is sacked around middle of tour

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece
sacked in the sense of plundered or ravaged, so these letters are thrown into disorder
the middle of the word tour, its central pair of characters

explanation.surface: A dreadful performer gets fired partway through a theatre tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges ACTOR IS into ATROCIS; 'around' wraps it round the centre of 'tour'. 'Terrible actor' tempts as a phrase, but 'Terrible' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atrocious is appalling or of very poor quality.

clue.text: Troops reach island, one in the South Pacific

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve troops
to reach a target is to hit it

explanation.surface: Soldiers land on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' looks like the definition but gives I; the definition is 'one in the South Pacific'. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This French Polynesian island lies in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Slash the cost of delicate fabric

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Cutting the price of fine material.
explanation.walkthrough: The lace rate is the cost of lace, so the pieces come in that order; 'of' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or cut flesh deeply.

clue.text: Greek no-frills vacation is free of charge

indicators.note: stripped of its frills, only the central core of the word vacation remains

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A budget Greek holiday that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-frills' strips the outsides of VACATION repeatedly to leave its middle two letters, AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without payment, costing nothing.

clue.text: I'm staying in church a long time — fancy

indicators.note: staying in means remaining inside, so the I'm piece sits within the others

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone lingering in church for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying in' signals the container; 'fancy' is a noun here, a flight of imagination, not a verb or adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or fantasy, from the mythical hybrid monster.

clue.text: US resort with a hut for natives

parts.note: Miami is a Florida resort city

explanation.surface: A Florida holiday town with a local cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mia-mia is a traditional Aboriginal Australian shelter of bark and branches.

clue.text: Desire to marry in East End of London?

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops initial aitches, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: to get hitched is to marry, so hitch means wed

explanation.surface: A question about wanting to wed in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, traditionally drop the H sound, so HITCH becomes 'ITCH. 'East End' tempts you to take the last letter of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or urge.

clue.text: Breathing space in flight

explanation.surface: A pause for breath during an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links. The first sense is an anatomical airway; the second is a trip by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is a channel through which we breathe; travel by aircraft is passage by air.

clue.text: Dramatically produces case for violin

indicators.note: the word dramatically acts as a case holding the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Something theatrically makes a box for a fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces case for' tells you 'Dramatically' encases the answer. Amati was a family of Cremona violin makers, so an Amati is one of their instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments by the Amati family of Cremona are prized fiddles.

clue.text: Run fast, being short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the time abbreviation is removed

parts.note: fleet means swift

explanation.surface: Sprinting while running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run fast' looks like the definition, but 'fast' gives FLEET; 'short of' removes T; 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or run away.

clue.text: Does extra hours working at introduction to atonal musical piece

parts.note: someone who moonlights works a second job outside normal hours
a machine that is on is working
taken as written

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening character

explanation.surface: Putting in overtime on a piece of music without a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The overtime picture conceals MOONLIGHTS + ON + AT + A, the A being the first letter of 'atonal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 is popularly known by this nickname.

clue.text: The writer with the golden gun

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: An allusion to a Bond villain with a gilded firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Bond film The Man with the Golden Gun. The Sten was a British submachine gun of World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen was the English novelist of Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Entering a seedy joint, man's intended to stay put?

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the man's piece goes inside the others

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
man's reads as he's, a contraction of he is

explanation.surface: A man walks into a sleazy bar intending to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' signals the container. The question mark flags the playful definition: glue is made to keep things in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is designed to make things stick fast where they are placed.
